description:
Mesh non-orthogonality in the cfmesh pipeline traces to the TET PRIMAL, not to the dual operation or the solver. Fix the tet mesher.

EVIDENCE THAT THE DUAL IS EXACT (measured 2026-08-07, test re-run and passing):
crates/outram-foam-mesh/tests/poly_dual_mesh.rs:212 dual_quality_is_exactly_orthogonal_on_a_uniform_block asserts max_non_ortho_deg < 1e-12, mean < 1e-12, max_skewness < 1e-12 (:226-232). Re-ran `cargo test -p outram-foam-mesh --release --test poly_dual_mesh`: 3^3 block -> 64 dual cells, non-orthogonality max 0.000 deg / mean 0.000 deg, skewness 0.0000, verdict GOOD; 4^3 block identical. The metric itself is closed-form validated in crates/outram-foam-mesh/src/mesh_quality.rs:600 (Cartesian block = 0) and :651 (sheared block matches atan(k) at 45/60/86 deg to 1e-10).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- that test is NOT of cfmesh's dual. It exercises outram_foam_mesh::poly_dual_mesh, the CELL-CENTRE polyDualMesh (poly_dual_mesh.rs:25-41). cfmesh uses a DIFFERENT algorithm, the median/Donald vertex-centred dual (crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/dual.rs:48-70, which says so explicitly). cfmesh's four dual tests (dual.rs:441, :474, :499, :543) check only closure, volume conservation, boundary match and face count. So "the dual is exact" is MEASURED for outram-foam-mesh's dual and only INFERRED for cfmesh's.
=> First sub-task: add an orthogonality test for cfmesh's own median dual on a uniform block. Until that exists the diagnosis is one step short of proven.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT THE TET PRIMAL:
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/tet.rs:93 pub fn tetrahedralize(mesh: &VolumeMesh) -- centroid subdivision (every cell -> cell.face.edge tets). Its two tests (tet.rs:169, :197) assert ONLY positive volume, closedness, boundary area = 6, volume = 1, 4 triangular faces per cell. No non-orthogonality or skewness metric is asserted on the tet primal anywhere in the tree.
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/delaunay.rs:42-44 states the defect qualitatively: centroid subdivision "is not a Delaunay one -- some interior faces fail the empty-circumsphere (locally-Delaunay) test, which is what leaves slivers."
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/pipeline.rs:774-775 records uniform 0.40 m -> max non-orth 85.14 deg and uniform 0.30 m -> 85.38 deg, and :804-805 notes those runs "report polyhedral dual skipped -- their output is the tetrahedralization". Dualised rows at the same geometry measure 71.7-72.5 deg. This supports the direction of the claim.
  CAVEAT: those ~85 deg figures are DOC-RECORDED, not test-asserted. The test at pipeline.rs:812 runs only two of the eight table rows and asserts merely max_non_orthogonality_deg < 90.0 (:842). Do not cite 85.14/85.38 as measured-by-CI.

WORK:
1. Add an orthogonality/skewness test for cfmesh's median dual on a uniform block (close the inference gap above).
2. Add non-orthogonality + skewness metrics to the tet primal tests in tet.rs.
3. Replace or repair centroid subdivision with a locally-Delaunay tetrahedralization (see delaunay.rs) so slivers are removed at source.

NOTED TENSION: the same fleet added a solver-side non-orthogonal correction -- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvm/laplacian_corrected.rs (untracked) and crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/tests/non_orthogonal_laplacian.rs. So "do not chase a solver-side correction" is an editorial recommendation the tree currently contradicts. The maintainer should decide whether that correction stays (it is legitimate OpenFOAM practice regardless) -- the point of this bead is that it must not be treated as a SUBSTITUTE for fixing the tet mesher.
title: cfmesh: fix tet-primal mesh quality — it is the real non-orthogonality source, not the dual

description: The digitiser (op-5v5.8) is currently verified by SYNTHETIC self-consistency only (tests/digitiser_synthetic.rs; measured 2026-08-11: max 0.138 percent of y-span on lin-lin and log-lin, max 0.002765 decades on log-log, 455 points each). No accuracy claim exists against real published figures. When the maintainer supplies the hand-digitised Tobias decay-heat points (op-amfh), add a test/example that: (1) runs kovan-digitise over the same figure scans with the calibration recorded in the oracle data, (2) interpolates the digitiser output at the oracle x values in log-log space (the interp_loglog helper in tests/digitiser_synthetic.rs::oracle_comparison_shape is the intended shape), (3) asserts agreement within a stated tolerance that accounts for the oracle's own reading uncertainty, and (4) documents methodology + measured numbers per the workspace V and V rule. Note the Tobias PDF (kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf) is likely proprietary-tier; the digitised POINTS are facts and can be committed with provenance, the scans themselves must respect the open/proprietary split.
title: kovan-literature digitiser: run the Tobias golden-oracle comparison when op-amfh lands

description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'we should have a standard HP and LP turbine as it is for the PWR plants' -- in the widget library.

CORRECTION THIS CARRIES. On 2026-08-04 the mirrored 'hourglass' silhouette inherited from fhr_sim_v2 was called an artwork defect and replaced with monotonic inlet-to-exhaust blade growth (commit b44f549). That was only half right. A PWR LP turbine is normally DOUBLE-FLOW: steam admits at the centre and expands outward in BOTH directions, so its rotor genuinely is mirrored about the mid-plane. The real defect was applying one silhouette unconditionally, plus proportions that collapsed at wide aspect ratios. Flow path is a property of the machine, not a drawing style.

WHAT TO BUILD:
  - Single-flow: monotonic expansion, inlet one end, exhaust the other. Typical HP.
  - Double-flow: centre admission, mirrored expansion to an exhaust at each end. Typical PWR LP, and how the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork was actually shaped.

Closed set -> enum dispatch, per the workspace no-trait-objects rule.

STANDARD PWR SECONDARY ARRANGEMENT to represent:
  - Steam generators deliver SATURATED (not superheated) steam, roughly 6-7 MPa.
  - HP turbine expands to roughly 1 MPa. Wet steam throughout, so erosion matters.
  - A moisture separator reheater (MSR) sits between HP and LP -- it is a distinct component and is NOT currently in the widget library at all. Worth its own bead.
  - Typically two or three double-flow LP turbines exhaust to the condenser at vacuum (~5 kPa).
  - LP last-stage blades are very long; the annulus area ratio between HP and LP is large and should be visible when the two widgets are shown side by side.

RELATION TO OTHER BEADS: per-stage blade angulation and the impulse/reaction mix are op-wqk.14.11 (placeholders now, real angles when the physical turbine model lands, op-dt3.18). Physical envelope dimensions remain blocked on op-dt3.17.1. This bead is about the FLOW PATH and the HP/LP presets, which are independent of both.

DO NOT present the presets as a specific vendor's or plant's design -- they are illustrative standard-arrangement values per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md, and the data policy forbids using any actual plant data.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-04 (maintainer): DOUBLE-FLOW IS THE DEFAULT for turbine widgets. Single-flow remains available as the other enum variant, but a TurbineVisual built without specifying a flow path draws double-flow.

This matches large-PWR practice rather than being merely a drawing preference: at PWR secondary-side volumetric flows, the HP turbine is commonly double-flow as well as the LP set (a typical large PWR turbine-generator is one double-flow HP plus two or three double-flow LP cylinders). So double-flow is the right default for BOTH presets, not just LP.

Practical consequence for the implementation: the mirrored silhouette from the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork becomes the DEFAULT rendering again, with centre admission and an exhaust at each end -- but now with the pitch-derived proportions from b44f549 so it no longer collapses at wide aspect ratios, and with the blade-height growth running outward from the centre admission plane toward both exhausts (not inward, and not mirrored-by-accident as before).

title: Widget library: standard PWR HP and LP turbines (single-flow vs double-flow)
